title: Two credential grades: a run gets read-only or write, and never picks its own
description:
D11's second grade, and the contract the rest of Phase 4 rests on — so it lands first and alone.

Everything the factory runs today gets a credential that can push. Phase 4 introduces runs that must NOT: a PR review run reads a diff and comments, and giving it write access to the branch it is reviewing is the kind of blast radius that is obvious in hindsight.

Deliverable: a run declares its grade at submission, the control plane mints the matching credential, and the grade is a property of the RUN RECORD rather than of the prompt. A read-only run that tries to push must fail at the credential, not at an instruction it was asked to respect — Phase 3's dxk learning applies directly: a boundary the substrate can enforce must not rest on instruction-following.

Watch the interaction with vdg: the shipped GitHub rung is a user-to-server token whose permissions come from the App installation, so 'read-only' may need to be enforced at the factory rather than expressed in the token. Say which, and if it is the factory, say what stops a run from simply calling GitHub directly.
acceptance_criteria: A run's grade is recorded on the run and drives the credential it is issued; a read-only run cannot push, proven by attempting it rather than by reading the code; the enforcement point is documented.
